insight.title: How Light Paints the World
insight.subtitle: The quiet dialogue between the sun and our eyes.

sections.text: Every morning, the world emerges from a deep, velvet shadow. We wake to a room filled with color, yet color does not live inside the objects themselves. Instead, it is a fleeting gift from the sun. Without the gentle touch of traveling beams, the red apple and the blue sea are exactly the same.

Science tells us that light travels in tiny, silent waves. When these waves strike a surface, the object keeps some for itself and reflects others back to us. Your eyes catch these wandering rays, turning them into a signal. In that instant, your mind builds a vibrant map of the space around you.

This means you never truly touch the world with your hands alone. You perceive it through a constant, shimmering rain of energy. It is a reminder that we are deeply connected to the stars. We are not just observers of the light; we are the very place where the universe finally sees itself.

news.title: Manipal Hospital launches adaptive deep brain stimulation at Sarjapur Road
news.description: Manipal Hospital, Sarjapur Road, has launched Adaptive Deep Brain Stimulation (aDBS) for movement disorders. This advanced system monitors brain activity and adjusts stimulation in real-time, offering improved symptom control and reduced side effects. The technology, utilizing BrainSense to analyze beta waves, aims to enhance patient quality of life, particularly for those with Parkinson's disease unresponsive to medication.

news.title: New "super antibiotic" stops deadly gut infection without destroying the microbiome
news.description: A newly developed antibiotic called EVG7 could offer a powerful new way to stop Clostridioides difficile, a dangerous gut bacterium that often returns after treatment. In mouse studies, researchers found that even a very small dose of EVG7 was highly effective at clearing the infection and preventing it from coming back. Unlike many current antibiotics, which wipe out large portions of the gut microbiome, EVG7 appears to spare beneficial bacteria that naturally help keep C. difficile in check.
